question: why do people with mental health issues smoke so much?
answer: Individuals with behavioral health conditions are more likely to smoke, accounting for 38% of all U.S. adult cigarette consumption, despite making up only 25% of the population. This group has a smoking rate of 23%, higher than the general adult rate of 14%.
